rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A unit vector is not the number 1. It has a direction.  ·  Equal vectors need not share a point of application.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: î, ĵ, k̂ are mutually perpendicular.  ·  A zero vector cannot define a direction for a unit vector.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A zero vector has magnitude zero and no direction. It is the resultant of two equal and opposite vectors. Adding it to a vector leaves that vector unchanged.  ·  A unit vector has magnitude 1 and points in a chosen direction. If A is a non-zero vector, the unit vector along it is Â = A / |A|. The symbols î, ĵ and k̂ are unit vectors along the coordinate axes.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The zero vector is not a unit vector.  ·  î has magnitude 1. A component such as 3î has magnitude 3.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Equal vectors have the same magnitude and the same direction. They need not act at the same point. A negative of a vector has the same magnitude and the opposite direction. Multiplying by −1 produces it.  ·  Collinear vectors lie along the same line or along parallel lines. Like collinear vectors point the same way. Unlike collinear vectors point opposite ways.  ·  A position vector of a point is drawn from the chosen origin to that point. It locates the point. A displacement vector joins two positions and does not have to start at the origin.
